svg.aria-label: The three recorded runs of Experiment 01. Two ran at a target of 60 journeys per second and one at 30. Success rate, 95th-percentile journey latency and HTTP failure rate are shown per run. The knee of roughly 35 journeys per second quoted in the experiment README comes from a separate Civo run and is shown as a stated finding, not derived from these.

svg.text: Full checkout journey (cart -> add item -> booking -> conversion) at a ramping arrival rate, 3 x (2 OCPU / 16 GB) nodes, booking + inventory HPA 1..4.

svg.text: The knee sits at ~35 journeys/s on Civo, where the nodes reach 93% CPU (~320m of CPU per journey).

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Past it the degradation is latency, not errors. TARGET_RPS=60 is unreachable on that cluster and

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: shows up as VU starvation, not as system failure.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: RESULTS.md leaves "Achieved throughput (journeys/s)" empty in all three runs, so a throughput-vs-latency curve cannot be drawn from what is committed.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Run k6 with --summary-export=summary.json and the curve becomes derivable — see assets/_toolkit/exp01_runs.py.
